title: Surah Al-Fātiḥah (The Opening, The Preface, or The Starter)
subtitle: Makkan · 7 Verses
snippet: Guidance, worship, and the straight path
keywords: 1 Al-Fātiḥah Al-Fatihah الفاتحة The Opening, The Preface, or The Starter Makkan Guidance, worship, and the straight path This Surah is the undeniable essence, the summary, and the master key of the entire Quran. It is a perfectly structured, divine script that teaches human beings exactly how to approach, praise, and talk to their Creator, culminating in the single most important request a human can ever make: the plea for guidance.

title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow or The Heifer)
subtitle: Madinan · 286 Verses
snippet: Faith, law, trials, and building a Muslim society
keywords: 2 Al-Baqarah Al-Baqarah البقرة The Cow or The Heifer Madinan Faith, law, trials, and building a Muslim society This Surah is the foundational constitution of Islam, transitioning believers from a persecuted minority to a governing society. But beyond its laws, it is a massive archive of human history. It uses vivid, detailed stories of past prophets, kings, and ordinary people to teach the new Muslim community how to avoid the fatal mistakes of arrogance, doubt, and disobedience.

title: Surah Āl-'Imrān (The Family of Imran (Imran is the father of Maryam/Mary, making this the family of Jesus).)
subtitle: Madinan · 200 Verses
keywords: 3 Āl-'Imrān Al-'Imran آل عمران The Family of Imran (Imran is the father of Maryam/Mary, making this the family of Jesus). Madinan Steadfastness, truth of Islam, unity While Surah Al-Baqarah was about building the foundation of the Muslim nation, Surah Ali 'Imran is about steadfastness (Thabat). It teaches the believers how to stay firm when facing external ideological attacks (theological debates about God and Jesus) and internal physical and psychological crises (the heartbreaking defeat and loss of life at Uhud).

title: Surah An-Nisā (The Women)
subtitle: Madinan · 176 Verses
snippet: Social justice, family law, women's rights
keywords: 4 An-Nisā An-Nisa النساء The Women Madinan Social justice, family law, women's rights If Surah Al-Baqarah was about building the nation and Surah Ali 'Imran was about defending it, Surah An-Nisa is about social justice and protecting the vulnerable. It establishes the internal laws of a healthy society, dismantling the oppressive practices of pre-Islamic Arabia. It focuses heavily on the rights of women, orphans, the distribution of wealth, eradicating hypocrisy, and establishing absolute, unflinching justice.

title: Surah Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread or The Table Spread with Food)
subtitle: Madinan · 120 Verses
keywords: 5 Al-Mā'idah Al-Ma'idah المائدة The Table Spread or The Table Spread with Food Madinan Law, covenants, halal & haram If Surah Al-Baqarah built the nation, Ali 'Imran defended it, and An-Nisa established its internal social justice, Surah Al-Ma'idah is the grand finale. Its core theme is Covenants and Completion. It establishes the final, uncompromising dietary, legal, and social laws of Islam, finalizes the theological boundaries with the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), and celebrates the absolute perfection of the religion.

title: Surah Al-An'ām (The Cattle or The Grazing Livestock)
subtitle: Makkan · 165 Verses
keywords: 6 Al-An'ām Al-An'am الأنعام The Cattle or The Grazing Livestock Makkan Tawḥīd and rejecting shirk This Surah is the ultimate, masterclass defense of Tawhid (the absolute Oneness of God). It systematically dismantles idolatry, superstition, and arrogance using logic, nature, and the history of past prophets. It is designed to arm the believer with unshakable intellectual and spiritual proof that Allah is the only true Sovereign over the universe.

title: Surah Al-A'rāf (The Heights or The Elevations)
subtitle: Makkan · 206 Verses
snippet: Stories of prophets and consequences of arrogance
keywords: 7 Al-A'rāf Al-A'raf الأعراف The Heights or The Elevations Makkan Stories of prophets and consequences of arrogance This Surah is an epic, sweeping historical narrative. It traces the journey of humanity from our creation in heaven, to our descent to Earth, through the rise and fall of ancient civilizations (Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb, and Musa), all the way to our final destinations on the Day of Judgment. It heavily focuses on the tactics of Iblis (Satan), warning us not to fall for the same traps that destroyed the nations of the past.

title: Surah Al-Anfāl (The Spoils of War, The Bounties, or Voluntary Gifts)
subtitle: Madinan · 75 Verses
keywords: 8 Al-Anfāl Al-Anfal الأنفال The Spoils of War, The Bounties, or Voluntary Gifts Madinan Battle of Badr, divine help The Surah is a masterclass in the spiritual physics of victory. It completely deconstructs the human obsession with material wealth (the spoils of war) and physical military strategy. Instead, it redefines true victory as a divine gift granted only to a community that maintains absolute unity, sincere trust in God (Tawakkul), and spiritual discipline in the face of impossible odds.

title: Surah At-Tawbah (The Repentance (It is also widely known as Surah Al-Bara'ah, meaning The Disavowal or The Ultimatum).)
subtitle: Madinan · 129 Verses
keywords: 9 At-Tawbah At-Tawbah التوبة The Repentance (It is also widely known as Surah Al-Bara'ah, meaning The Disavowal or The Ultimatum). Madinan Hypocrisy exposed, sincerity in faith This Surah is the ultimate stress test for the Muslim community. It acts as a divine filter, completely exposing the hypocrites who were hiding within the ranks. It establishes the final, uncompromising laws regarding treaties and warfare, and it provides a masterclass on the psychology of true, sincere repentance.

title: Surah Yūnus (Jonah (Named after the Prophet Yunus/Jonah).)
subtitle: Makkan · 109 Verses
keywords: 10 Yūnus Yunus يونس Jonah (Named after the Prophet Yunus/Jonah). Makkan Mercy, repentance, belief This Surah is a masterclass in divine wisdom and mercy. It defends the authenticity of the Quran against accusations of magic or forgery, analyzes the fickle nature of human psychology during hardship versus ease, and powerfully contrasts two historical examples of facing God's punishment: the rejected repentance of Pharaoh versus the accepted, unprecedented repentance of the people of Yunus.

title: Surah Hūd (The Prophet Hud (Named after the Prophet sent to the ancient, powerful tribe of 'Ad).)
subtitle: Makkan · 123 Verses
keywords: 11 Hūd Hud هود The Prophet Hud (Named after the Prophet sent to the ancient, powerful tribe of 'Ad). Makkan Patience through trials This Surah is an emotional and theological anchor. It focuses heavily on Istiqamah (unwavering steadfastness). Through vivid, detailed, and often heartbreaking stories of past Prophets - Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, and Shu'ayb - it teaches the believers that while the path of truth is filled with intense loneliness, mockery, and struggle, God's perfect justice will ultimately rescue the righteous and crush the arrogant.

title: Surah Yūsuf (Joseph (Named after the Prophet Yusuf/Joseph).)
subtitle: Makkan · 111 Verses
keywords: 12 Yūsuf Yusuf يوسف Joseph (Named after the Prophet Yusuf/Joseph). Makkan Trust Allah in hardship This Surah is entirely unique in the Quran. While other chapters weave various themes and stories together, Surah Yusuf is dedicated entirely to a single, continuous, highly detailed narrative from beginning to end. It is a profound masterclass in dealing with grief, navigating family betrayal, maintaining absolute integrity in the face of temptation, and trusting that Allah's intricate, hidden plan (Al-Latif) will always lead to ultimate victory for those who practice "beautiful patience.

title: Surah Ar-Ra'd (The Thunder)
subtitle: Disputed · 43 Verses
keywords: 13 Ar-Ra'd Ar-Ra'd الرعد The Thunder Disputed Truth vs falsehood This Surah is a breathtaking display of Allah's power over the natural world. It establishes that the truth of Islam is as undeniable, heavy, and life-giving as rain, while falsehood is as temporary and empty as foam. It beautifully contrasts the terrifying, majestic power of thunderstorms with the deep, quiet peace that a believer's heart finds in the remembrance of God.

title: Surah Ibrāhīm (Abraham (Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him))
subtitle: Makkan · 52 Verses
keywords: 14 Ibrāhīm Ibrahim إبراهيم Abraham (Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him) Makkan Gratitude and du'ā This Surah is a powerful message of light, gratitude, and unshakable faith. Revealed when the Muslims were weak and mocked, it reminds believers that Allah's message brings people out of darkness into light. Through the stories of past prophets, a chilling speech from Shaytan on Judgment Day, and the heartfelt prayers of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), it teaches that gratitude brings endless blessings, while arrogance and ingratitude lead to total ruin.

title: Surah Al-Ḥijr (The Rocky Tract or The Stoneland (referring to the mountainous valley inhabited by the ancient tribe of Thamud).)
subtitle: Makkan · 99 Verses
keywords: 15 Al-Ḥijr Al-Hijr الحجر The Rocky Tract or The Stoneland (referring to the mountainous valley inhabited by the ancient tribe of Thamud). Makkan Qur'an's protection, arrogance of Iblīs This Surah is a powerful reassurance of Allah's absolute control and protection. Revealed when the Prophet (pbuh) was mocked and called mad by the leaders of Makkah, it guarantees that Allah Himself will guard the Quran forever. Through the stories of Adam and Iblis, Prophet Ibrahim, Prophet Lut, and the ruined stone cities of Al-Hijr, it proves that no fortress, wealth, or arrogance can ever protect wrongdoers from Allah's decree, while sincere believers are shielded by His mercy.

title: Surah An-Naḥl (The Bee (An-Nahl))
subtitle: Makkan · 128 Verses
keywords: 16 An-Naḥl An-Nahl النحل The Bee (An-Nahl) Makkan Allah's blessings and gratitude Known by classical scholars as Surah an-Ni'am ("The Chapter of Blessings"), this Surah is a sweeping tour of Allah's countless favors - from rain, oceans, and livestock to homes, families, and the healing honey of the bee. Its core message is simple and direct: every single comfort in human life comes from Allah alone, so worshipping powerless idols or showing ingratitude is completely illogical. It calls humanity to pure monotheism, justice, patience, and deep thankfulness.

title: Surah Al-Isrā (The Night Journey (Al-Isra) - also famously known in early Hadith collections as Surah Bani Israel (The Children of Israel).)
subtitle: Makkan · 111 Verses
keywords: 17 Al-Isrā Al-Isra الإسراء The Night Journey (Al-Isra) - also famously known in early Hadith collections as Surah Bani Israel (The Children of Israel). Makkan Ethics, responsibility This Surah is a breathtaking transition from deep earthly grief to heavenly honor. Revealed after the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) endured his hardest year of personal loss and fierce rejection, it opens by glorifying Allah for taking him from Makkah to Jerusalem in a single night. Alongside a comprehensive moral charter for human society - covering kindness to parents, justice, modesty, and honesty - it recounts pivotal stories of the Children of Israel, the rebellion of Iblis, Prophet Musa's nine miracles, and the ultimate honor awaiting Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) on the Day of Judgment.

title: Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave (Al-Kahf))
subtitle: Makkan · 110 Verses
keywords: 18 Al-Kahf Al-Kahf الكهف The Cave (Al-Kahf) Makkan Trials of faith, knowledge, power This Surah is the ultimate spiritual shield against the four greatest trials (fitnah) of human life: the trial of faith, the trial of wealth, the trial of knowledge, and the trial of power. Through four unforgettable stories - the Youths of the Cave, the Owner of the Two Gardens, Prophet Musa and Al-Khidr, and the righteous king Dhul-Qarnayn - it teaches believers how to stay humble, patient, and anchored in Allah until the very end of time.

title: Surah Maryam (Mary (Maryam, peace be upon her - the only chapter in the entire Quran named after a woman).)
subtitle: Makkan · 98 Verses
keywords: 19 Maryam Maryam مريم Mary (Maryam, peace be upon her - the only chapter in the entire Quran named after a woman). Makkan Mercy and miracles This Surah is a tender, deeply moving showcase of Allah's boundless mercy (Ar-Rahman is mentioned 16 times - more than in any other Surah). Revealed when the early Muslims were being tortured and forced to flee their homes, it tells the miraculous stories of Prophet Zakariya, Maryam, Prophet 'Isa, Prophet Ibrahim, and earlier prophets to prove that nothing is impossible for Allah, pure monotheism is the true message of all prophets, and Allah always protects and loves His sincere servants.

title: Surah Ṭā-Hā (Ta-Ha (named after the two Arabic opening letters Ta and Ha, whose exact meaning is known only to Allah).)
subtitle: Makkan · 135 Verses
keywords: 20 Ṭā-Hā Ta-Ha طه Ta-Ha (named after the two Arabic opening letters Ta and Ha, whose exact meaning is known only to Allah). Makkan Comfort to the Prophet (pbuh) This Surah is a deeply comforting message that the Quran was revealed to bring mercy, guidance, and inner peace - not misery. Through the most detailed life story of Prophet Musa (AS) in the Quran and the story of Prophet Adam (AS), it teaches that Allah never abandons His sincere servants, that falsehood always collapses before truth, and that real contentment comes only from remembering Allah.

title: Surah Al-Anbiyā (The Prophets (Al-Anbiya))
subtitle: Makkan · 112 Verses
keywords: 21 Al-Anbiyā Al-Anbiya الأنبياء The Prophets (Al-Anbiya) Makkan Unity of prophets' message This Surah is a powerful wake-up call about the nearness of the Day of Judgment, the Oneness of Allah (Tawhid), and the shared brotherhood of all prophets. Because the leaders of Makkah mocked Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) for being an ordinary human being, Allah brings together the stories of sixteen prophets in one chapter - proving that every messenger was human, faced severe trials, called people to One God, and was rescued by Allah through sincere prayer and patience.

title: Surah Al-Ḥajj (The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj))
subtitle: Madinan · 78 Verses
keywords: 22 Al-Ḥajj Al-Hajj الحج The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj) Madinan Worship and sacrifice This Surah is a powerful reminder of the terror of the Final Hour, the undeniable proofs of Resurrection, and the true spirit of devotion to Allah. Revealed as the persecuted Muslims were driven out of Makkah and barred from the Kaaba, it revives the pure legacy of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), grants the oppressed believers their very first permission to defend themselves, and dismantles idol worship through unforgettable parables.

title: Surah Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers (Al-Mu'minun))
subtitle: Makkan · 118 Verses
keywords: 23 Al-Mu'minūn Al-Mu'minun المؤمنون The Believers (Al-Mu'minun) Makkan Qualities of true believers This Surah defines what true, lasting success actually looks like. While the arrogant leaders of Makkah measured success by wealth, power, and social status, Allah opens this chapter by declaring that the true winners are the sincere believers who guard their prayers, character, and trusts. Through the miracle of human creation, the stories of past prophets, and a haunting conversation on the Day of Judgment, it proves that life has a serious purpose and that real victory belongs only to faith and righteousness.

title: Surah An-Nūr (The Light (An-Nur))
subtitle: Madinan · 64 Verses
keywords: 24 An-Nūr An-Nur النور The Light (An-Nur) Madinan Modesty, morality, social purity This Surah is the divine shield that protects the honor, purity, and peace of Muslim families and communities. Revealed at a moment when hypocrites tried to tear Madinah apart from within through vicious gossip and slander against the Prophet's own household, it lays down clear moral laws, rules of privacy and modesty, and the breathtaking parable of Allah's Light - teaching that true light illuminates both the heart and the home.

title: Surah Al-Furqān (The Criterion (Al-Furqan - that which clearly separates truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, and right from wrong).)
subtitle: Makkan · 77 Verses
keywords: 25 Al-Furqān Al-Furqan الفرقان The Criterion (Al-Furqan - that which clearly separates truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, and right from wrong). Makkan Truth vs falsehood This Surah is a powerful defense of the Quran and the humanity of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Revealed when the pagan leaders of Makkah ridiculed the Prophet (pbuh) for being an ordinary human who ate food and walked in the markets, it dismantles every excuse of arrogance, warns against toxic friendships that lead to eternal regret, and closes with a breathtaking portrait of the true "Servants of the Most Merciful" ('Ibad ar-Rahman).

title: Surah Ash-Shu'arā (The Poets (Ash-Shu'ara))
subtitle: Makkan · 227 Verses
keywords: 26 Ash-Shu'arā Ash-Shu'ara الشعراء The Poets (Ash-Shu'ara) Makkan Prophets vs rejection This Surah is a powerful consolation for Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a sweeping proof that the Quran is pure divine revelation - not human poetry or magic. By walking through seven major prophetic stories in a rhythmic pattern - each ending with the exact same refrain, "Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not to be believers. And indeed, your Lord - He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful" - it proves that every prophet was mocked, every arrogant nation was destroyed, and Allah always rescues His sincere servants.

title: Surah An-Naml (The Ant (An-Naml))
subtitle: Makkan · 93 Verses
keywords: 27 An-Naml An-Naml النمل The Ant (An-Naml) Makkan Gratitude and wisdom This Surah is a breathtaking display of Allah's complete knowledge, unseen wisdom, and absolute sovereignty over every creature - from the tiniest ant to the grandest kingdoms on earth. Through the stories of Prophet Musa, Prophet Sulayman, the Queen of Sheba, Prophet Salih, and Prophet Lut, it teaches that true greatness is found in humility and gratitude to Allah, while arrogance and plotting against the truth always end in ruin.

subtitle: Makkan · 88 Verses
